newsitem.title: FRANCE: Colombia's Ocampo urges coffee growers to up sales.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ocampo urges coffee growers to up sales.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said on Thursday leading producers should increase sales quotas or anticipate a part of their quota for later in the year in order to put downward pressure on prices.

But he warned in an interview with Reuters that prices must remain above $1.30 to $1.40 a pound if the world wants good-quality coffees, and said that previous prices of $1.00 to $1.10 were "not sufficient" to assure quality.
"I think it is not good for the producing countries. Too high a price like we were starting to get is bad because it hurts consumption," he said.
"I think the prices now are a bit high, but they were too low if the world wants quality coffee," Ocampo said during a visit to Paris aimed at encouraging French investment in Colombia.
"Many times we have delayed or anticipated sales, but it has to be negotiated, to assure discipline within the organisation (of coffee producing countries)," he said.

But he added he believed that increased sales by private Colombian exporters during the first quarter -- in anticipation of their second-quarter quotas -- had helped bring down prices a little from their recent highs.
About seven to 10 days ago, Colombia "allowed private exporters to anticipate part of that quota for the early part of the second quarter," he said.
While there was room for prices to fall, it was nonetheless important to keep prices high enough over the long term to cover the costs of producing quality beans, he added.
"If we cannot keep in the long run a price of $1.30 to $1.40 a pound, we cannot keep good quality," he said. "A dollar or $1.10 is not sufficient...Quality coffee cannot be produced at $1 a pound."
